label: rejected

evidence.V1: Three-quarter and silhouette read as a gable roof (triangular end, ridge cap), but the straight-on front view reads as a flat slate wall on a timber plinth.
evidence.V2: Big prism, medium ridge cap / slate courses / eave board, but no small tier; the gable end is a large blank flat brown triangle with no boards, vent or trim detail.
evidence.V3: Shallow, even pitch with long uniform brick-like slates and a plain filled gable gives a stiff, primitive read rather than a confident stylised roof (no overhang flare or sag).
evidence.V4: Slates, ridge cap and timber eave/barge boards all carry consistent chamfers that catch light in the gable and shingle close-ups.
evidence.V5: Flat-light ridge close-up shows a small tooth/notch where a slate meets the ridge cap (503 cross-shell overlaps); otherwise clean, A17/A18 pass.
evidence.V6: Stone hue in 3 grey values plus timber brown secondary; basalt and brick colourways keep the same disciplined structure.
evidence.V7: 800 tris = module target 800 (at target, under 2000 ceiling).
evidence.V8: One LF_VertexColor material, stone + timber secondary, chamfers at kit scale - consistent with the modular spec.
evidence.V9: Studio line correct: Anchored, CollisionFidelity Default, CanTouch off, Color white, SmoothPlastic; T1 tiling along X passes with IoU 1.0.

evidence.V1: Gabled peak reads from three-quarter and silhouette (triangular end, ridge cap, stepped shingle edge); front view reads as a shingled slope.
evidence.V2: Ridge cap and timber gable/eave board (big/medium), shingle courses (medium), stepped shingle ends (small).
evidence.V3: Chunky stylised shingles with a believable pitch; nothing floats.
evidence.V4: Shingles, ridge and eave board carry consistent chamfers in the shingles close-up.
evidence.V5: Gable-end close-ups show cluttered overlapping shingle ends jammed at the top corner by the ridge, and the top view shows small brown specks of the base at the eave gaps.
evidence.V6: Slate in three values plus timber brown secondary; within kit limit, though the random light/dark shingle mix is busy.
evidence.V8: Single LF_VertexColor material, stone hue + timber secondary, chamfers: kit-consistent.
evidence.V9: Anchored, CollisionFidelity Default, CanTouch off, Color white, SmoothPlastic, grid-corner pivot; T1 pass.

evidence.V1: Three-quarter and silhouette read clearly as a gabled roof peak (pentagonal house outline with ridge cap), and the top view shows the ridge splitting two shingle slopes; front view is weaker (reads as a tiled panel) but still identifiable by the ridge cap.
evidence.V2: Big (two slopes + gable) and medium (staggered shingle courses, rounded ridge cap, timber eave and barge boards) are present, but the gable end is a large blank timber triangle and there is no small tier (no nails, notched shingle ends, finial).
evidence.V3: Rounded ridge cap and eave board help, but plain rectangular shingle slabs in regular courses and a flat triangular gable read fairly stiff; little exaggeration of overhang or ridge.
evidence.V4: Close_shingles, close_ridge and close_gable_end studio show consistent chamfers on shingle butts, ridge cap and barge/eave boards catching highlight lines.
evidence.V5: Close_ridge flat light shows a small stray sliver/spike on the top shingle edge just below the ridge cap, and the front view shows small timber-coloured slivers peeking through shingle joints near the ridge; A17/A18 pass otherwise.
evidence.V6: One stone/slate hue in three values plus a timber secondary in two values; brick and sandstone colourways keep the same structure.
evidence.V8: Single LF_VertexColor material, stone shingles + timber secondary per wave-2 modular spec, kit-range chamfers; matches kit.
evidence.V9: Studio line: Anchored, Default collision, CanTouch off, MeshPart white + SmoothPlastic, grid-corner pivot; T1 tiling passes (iou 1.0).

artifacts: small notch at a slate/ridge-cap junction visible in the flat ridge close-up
large flat untextured gable triangle reads as an empty panel
Jumbled overlapping shingle ends at the gable apex
Base colour peeking through shingle gaps at the eaves (top view)
Small stray sliver/spike on the shingle edge just under the ridge cap (close_ridge flat)
Timber-coloured slivers visible through shingle joints near the ridge in the front view
top_fixes: Break up the gable end: vertical boards, a timber frame or a small vent/round window, with a barge board that overhangs
Use shorter, chunkier lapped slates with clear course shadow lines so the slope stops reading as a brick wall
Clean the slate-to-ridge intersection so no notch shows in flat light
Clean the gable apex: trim shingle ends and let the ridge cap end flush with a bargeboard
Close eave gaps or colour the hidden base to match the shingles
Reduce value randomness of the shingles (favour mid value with occasional light/dark) to calm the surface
Remove the stray sliver under the ridge cap and close the shingle joints so the timber gable does not peek through
Detail the blank gable triangle (vertical boards, a vent, or a cross-beam) and add a small tier such as a ridge finial or nail heads
Order the shingle values and deepen the shingle butts / eave overhang for a more stylised, readable pitch
